Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — BenchProofer construction pipeline and the SWE-Proof benchmark (formal specs, axioms, reference implementations and proofs for the 500 SWE-bench Verified issues, extended to SWE-bench Pro); compares nine specification settings with one model (no spec, self-written formal/EARS spec, provided formal/EARS spec)

fields.v: Specification settings (Table 2 rows 0-8) under four specification backends: Nagini (contract-annotated Python, SMT), Velvet (imperative DSL in Lean, SMT), pure Lean 4 + Mathlib (agent-written proofs), and EARS structured natural-language requirements (no verifier; non-formal control). Versions pinned in Table 49: Nagini 1.2.0, Lean toolchain v4.24.0, Mathlib and Velvet by git revision (f897ebcf72cd, 2cf0acb04c51), z3 4.15.4, cvc5 1.3.1. EARS template version not stated
fields.why: Draft said verifier versions are not stated; Appendix Table 49 (p. 86) pins Nagini, Lean, Mathlib, Velvet and the SMT solvers.

fields.v: Formal specification (pre/postconditions over modeled functions) + axioms for unchanged callees + operation correspondence ('specification view'); implementation in the backend language with proof annotations; equivalent Python patch. EARS: requirements with numbered acceptance criteria in WHEN/THEN/SHALL, SHALL, IF/THEN, WHILE patterns (median 106 lines, 3.7 requirements, 14.7 criteria in the corpus)

Depends on setting: end-to-end (agent writes spec -> verifying implementation -> equivalent patch -> submit); from localization (same, given files/functions); from specification (given spec view -> verifying implementation -> patch); spec synthesis only (spec + witness implementation, no patch). Single ReAct loop (shell, verify, submit), 250-step budget
None during evaluation; grading by tests, verifier and LLM judges/auditors (majority of three). Authors hand-inspected some instances during construction
Specification artefact (formal or EARS) and its verification within one agent episode; full spec -> implementation -> patch flow in rows 2-3, 5, 7

Not classifiable (closest to spec-first: a per-issue spec is written or given before the implementation and is not maintained afterwards); authors' wording: 'formal specification', 'verified code generation', 'specification synthesis'
fields.why: 'Not stated' is not a value of the form (spec-first / spec-anchored / spec-as-source / not classifiable). The setting is a benchmark, not a development flow, so whether to call it spec-first or not classifiable is a judgement.

All: minimal ReAct scaffold (SWE-agent style) + Claude Opus 4.8, provider-default decoding, 250 steps; main values one run (Nagini cells repeated 4 times). Values %: Nagini / Velvet / Lean / EARS (Table 2, SWE-bench Verified, n = 500). Tokens = input tokens per episode (Table 41, Nagini unless noted). Draft verdict rule: quality works >= 90, partly 60-90, does not < 60; cost works <= 250k, partly 250-450k.

Repetitions (Nagini, Table 32): SD <= 1.3 points per cell

Tasks: SWE-bench Verified (500) and SWE-bench Pro Python (242). Configurations: 9 settings x 4 backends, one model (Claude Opus 4.8); 26 cells over 500 instances. Baselines: unaided (row 0), localization-only (row 4). Held constant: scaffold, prompts, 250-step budget, container, sanitized git history, hidden tests never visible. Acceptance tests: hidden SWE-bench tests plus verification and equivalence judges. Repetitions: 1 per cell; Nagini cells 4 (except rows 1, 5). Human intervention: none

Tests incomplete: 26.8 points of test-passing baseline patches overturned by audit (85.0 -> 58.2). Self-written spec does not help: row 2 vs row 0 +0.6 (Nagini) to -1.2. Provided formal spec raises resolution 85.0 -> 94.0-96.2; +6.9 over localization alone; +8.6 to +11.0 over self-written (row 7 vs 3). EARS: resolves like formal (row 2 EARS 421 vs Nagini 428, McNemar p = 0.35) but fails the audit far more (row 3: 286 vs 420 pass, p = 5e-28). Spec synthesis passes audit only 46-61%; faithfulness fails 42.5%. Unresolved instances' specs fail audit 92.3% vs 50.5% resolved. Cost: provided spec cheaper than end-to-end (389k vs 517k input tokens per resolved). Pro: provided spec below localization-only (55.8-59.9 vs 61.2)

Distinguished settings clearly on Verified; repetition SD <= 1.3 points, smaller than Wilson half-widths (1.66-4.37). Limitations stated: verify-implies-resolve rests on audited trust points (axiom soundness, implementation-patch refinement); backend expressiveness required manual modeling for a few instances; a few instances relax non-leakage; spec audit is an LLM panel (evidence, not proof); counterexample audit not applied to prover-accepted submissions, so EARS vs formal audit gap is not like-for-like

Faithful specification synthesis from informal intent is the open problem; trust points (axioms, refinement to Python patch, Python translation for conformance as weakest link); expressiveness limits (names, imports, class identity, process/filesystem effects cannot be specified; 22 Pro tasks refused); LLM auditors as evidence. Single model evaluated (not discussed as a limitation)

Artifacts and pipeline 'will be released' (no link), under MIT licence (p. 86). No pre-registration. Language: Python (specs in Python/Lean). Tool pins in Table 49 (p. 86). Inconsistencies: Table 32 says r1 is the Table 2 repetition, but Nagini r1 values differ for rows 2-8 (e.g., row 4 91.4 vs 88.2; row 8 49.2 vs 46.0 in Table 3), and Table 34 gives row 6 - row 0 = +11.4 vs 11.2 from Table 2; appendix F.3 says row 1 'has not been run' while Table 2 reports 58.2 and Table 18 lists one repetition; EARS row 3: F.3 gives 122 of 421 violations (29.0%, pass 59.8%), G.1 says 32% of resolving submissions, Table 2 gives 57.2% (286/500 in Table 40); '26.8% of the patches that pass' is a difference in points over all 500 (equals 31.5% of passing patches). Main text (p. 8) says EARS 'does not close' the gap and 'confers none of the improvement', but the appendix (p. 61) says the gap 'does not show that structured requirements are a weaker way to pin down behavior' because prover-accepted formal submissions were never audited. p. 86 says 'both models were reached through their providers' hosted APIs' although only Claude Opus 4.8 is evaluated; the model behind the LLM auditors/judges is not named. Values used from Table 2 (p. 7), Table 19 (p. 45), Table 41 (p. 62). AWS affiliation: Kiro (AWS) uses EARS, not mentioned in the paper (reviewer to judge)
fields.why: Added substantive reporting issues the draft missed: main-text EARS conclusion contradicted by the appendix caveat (p. 61), the 32% vs 29.0% figure, Table 34's +11.4, the 'both models' statement and unnamed judge model, and the Table 49 tool pins.
